questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L03_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which choice best shows a focused persuasive claim?

answer.text: A. Speeches happen in class

feedback.text: This is a topic statement, not a persuasive claim that takes a position.

answer.text: B. Students should rehearse speeches before presenting

feedback.text: Correct. This is a clear claim that can be supported with reasoning and evidence.

answer.text: C. Maybe presentations are sometimes hard

feedback.text: This is too uncertain to guide a persuasive argument.

answer.text: D. Speaking is a thing people do

feedback.text: This is vague and does not give the audience a clear position.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L03_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which choice best shows reasoning connected to a claim?

answer.text: A. Rehearsal is rehearsal

feedback.text: This repeats the idea and does not explain why it matters.

answer.text: B. Many people have speeches

feedback.text: This does not explain the value of rehearsal.

answer.text: C. The speech has a title

feedback.text: A title does not explain the claim about rehearsal.

answer.text: D. Rehearsal helps speakers find unclear parts before the audience hears them

feedback.text: Correct. This explains why rehearsal supports better speaking.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L03_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which choice best shows credible evidence?

answer.text: A. A timed practice run can show whether the introduction is too long

feedback.text: Correct. This concrete evidence supports the value of rehearsal.

answer.text: B. I just know rehearsal is best

feedback.text: This is personal certainty, not credible evidence.

answer.text: C. Someone somewhere said practice is fine

feedback.text: This source is vague and not trustworthy.

answer.text: D. The speaker likes note cards

feedback.text: Preference alone does not provide evidence for the claim.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L03_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which choice best shows evidence connection?

answer.text: A. The evidence is there, so it works

feedback.text: This does not explain the connection between evidence and claim.

answer.text: B. The claim is important because it is important

feedback.text: This repeats the idea instead of explaining it.

answer.text: C. This evidence supports the claim because timing helps speakers revise before presenting

feedback.text: Correct. This explains how the evidence proves the claim.

answer.text: D. The audience should agree automatically

feedback.text: An audience needs reasoning, not pressure to agree.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L03_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which choice best shows weak support?

answer.text: A. Practice is good because it is good

feedback.text: Correct. This is weak because it repeats instead of giving reasoning.

answer.text: B. Practice helps speakers notice unclear sections

feedback.text: This is stronger because it explains a specific benefit.

answer.text: C. A timed rehearsal can reveal pacing problems

feedback.text: This is specific evidence, not weak support.

answer.text: D. Rehearsal gives speakers a chance to revise

feedback.text: This explains how rehearsal helps, so it is not weak support.
